recommendation: Consider only if the pending quantum static-response candidate does not meet the target. No task or numerical prototype has been built.
apparatus: Independent mutually incoherent photon beams in a periodic uniform medium, all at the same known speed c=1. Known directions and positive background intensities, with specified infinitesimal sinusoidal intensity modulations. A constant unknown absorption rate kappa removes photons without scattering, emission, refraction, or feedback. Measure the signed first spatial Fourier component of total radiant energy or flux at a fixed time, normalized by the imposed infinitesimal modulation. Different beams propagate independently by the stated apparatus.
calibration: Spatially uniform modulations at several times and known nonzero background fluxes. All four lowest radiation moments decay exactly as exp(-kappa*t), independently of their angular closure. A nonzero total-energy calibration signal makes kappa globally identifiable. Fixed instrument uncertainty would be used.
completed_shortcut: The exact matrix-exponential solution of the linearized four-moment M1 radiation system about the known homogeneous beam background. It constructs E and F from every supplied beam direction and weight, uses the full nonlinear realizable Eddington tensor P(E,F) and its analytic Jacobian, then propagates the weak Fourier mode by a 4x4 generator. Absorption, conservation, characteristic speeds, flux direction and anisotropy of the M1 closure are all retained. The physical approximation is replacing angular structure by a positive boosted-isotropic distribution with the same E and F.
closure_definition: P=E[(1-chi)/2 I+(3chi-1)/2 n*n^T], f=|F|/E, n=F/|F|, chi=(3+4f^2)/(5+2*sqrt(4-3f^2)); at f=0 P=E I/3. Use an analytic derivative and the continuous f=0 limit; no finite-difference solver artifact is intended.
hidden_physics: Two or more independently propagating beams can have a pressure tensor that is not determined by E and F. Crossing or counterpropagating beams do not collide, although the coherent M1 closure can give the wrong transport of a known spatial modulation. The readout is ordinary radiant energy, not a thermodynamic heat/work interpretation.
analytic_separation: For equal counterpropagating beams along x with the same weak cos(kx) modulation, exact normalized energy response is exp(-kappa*t)*cos(k*t). The M1 linearization about F=0 instead gives exp(-kappa*t)*cos(k*t/sqrt(3)). At k*t=pi the true undamped amplitude is -1 and the M1 amplitude is approximately -0.241, well away from a zero-signal normalization. This is an analytic example, not a validated benchmark margin.
independent_reference: Direct characteristic transport of each beam: its complex Fourier amplitude is multiplied by exp[-(kappa+i*k dot direction)*t], then summed with the calibrated detector weights. A second reference can integrate each scalar transport equation or compare exact time derivatives against all known angular moments. Full-source validation would check weak-modulation positivity, flux conservation, real M1 wave speeds, single-beam and uniform-mode limits, and 256 noisy fits.
archive_overlap: Text inspection of archived/current apparatus and author files found no M1/Eddington/crossing-beam task. Archived phonon-transport also uses angular kinetics but tests conservation in the collision operator, while this tests angular pressure closure in independent ballistic propagation. Archived radiative-plates and film-transmission test boundary or energy-normalization effects. The broader partial-observability pattern is shared.
caveat: This is physically clean and distinct, but the exact beam-by-beam solution is simple once the physical approximation is noticed. Difficulty is unknown; no claim of Luna failure is justified. It should not replace an already qualifying task or motivate an unchanged rerun.
